Week 7 | Portfolio clustering with SephWide signals¶

PCA, K-Means and a transparent historical portfolio comparison¶

Ioannis Tzalas · MSc Banking & Finance · 5 November 2026

README and research question¶

Can price-derived risk and behaviour features organize stocks previously selected by SephWide into economically interpretable groups, and how did equal-weight portfolios of those groups behave over a later historical window?

The brief is titled DeFi Portfolio Clustering & Analysis, but its operative data requirement permits at least 50 assets/tokens. This submission uses US-listed equities previously selected by my SephWide algorithmic signal system. It is an equity application of the required methods; it makes no DeFi-token claim. If the lecturer intended tokens only, this scope needs their agreement.

Design frozen before this calculation: all distinct recorded BUY tickers dated on or before 1 September 2026, regardless of their subsequent performance. Fit period: 1 September 2023–1 September 2026. Later comparison: 2 September–21 October 2026. The complete declaration and download receipts are included. Earlier knowledge of this project and later-selected signal membership mean this is a conditional retrospective study, not a new prospective holdout.

SephWide's signals can influence real capital. Its exported strategy records and the portfolios constructed here are not authenticated funded-account fills or funded P&L. This assignment neither runs nor modifies SephWide.

Reproduce: the verified environment uses Python 3.14; pip install -r requirements.txt, open this notebook

Week 7 - Ioannis Tzalas¶

Start here¶

Submit W7_Portfolio_Clustering_Tzalas.ipynb, the executed notebook required by the brief. It contains all analysis code, outputs, written interpretation and inline figures. Keep the data/ folder with it for reproducibility. The HTML file is an offline readable copy. W7_Analysis_Report.pdf is a shorter companion report, not a substitute for the notebook.

This is the lecturer's PCA/K-Means portfolio assignment applied to 70 equities previously selected by SephWide. The brief permits “assets/tokens” although its title says DeFi. This is explicitly an equity application; clarify with the lecturer if tokens were intended exclusively. No trading project files are modified.

Measured results¶

  • 72 recorded BUY names through 1 September 2026, without filtering for winners.
  • NESR excluded for insufficient history; GOLD excluded for unresolved issuer identity after ticker reuse. All candidates and reasons remain in the data audit.
  • 70 assets, 787 price dates, 1 September 2023–21 October 2026.
  • 751 formation returns; 35 later comparison returns, 2 September–21 October 2026.
  • 3 PCs retain 82.71% of standardized asset-feature variation.
  • k=2 selected; silhouette 0.3881. The elbow suggests k=3, but it creates a single-stock group and fails the declared three-asset minimum.
  • Net later cumulative returns at 10 bps one-way costs: Cluster 1 -1.84%, Cluster 2 -2.96%, all-asset equal weights -2.05%, equal clusters -2.22%, SPY +1.53%. These are constructed historical portfolios, not funded P&L.
  • Full first-BUY illustration: 24 positive and 46 negative adjusted-price changes, with different holding lengths, no strategy exits and no execution claim. Five positive examples are explicitly selected retrospectively; losses remain.
  • 69 in-notebook structural checks and 439 separate numerical/submission checks. These do not establish predictive success or independent third-party assurance.

Important evidence limits and corrections¶

The first version admitted 71 names and was executed before the GOLD issuer problem was identified. The final 70-name version excludes it for identity, without mapping the signal to another company or optimizing on its return. The first notebook/results and timestamped identity receipt are retained. There are two analytical data versions, each containing 28 declared fits with 50 initializations: 56 distinct version-specific fits / 2,800 starts. Routine re-execution of the same fixed version is recorded separately and is not a new research variant.

The later comparison is conditional and retrospective, and was inspected during quality review. It is not an untouched or prospective holdout. No production candidate is proposed. Selection/survivorship, data vintage, only 35 evaluation sessions, model assumptions and simplified trading costs materially limit conclusions. The exported project records are strategy signals, not proof of funded execution. Source links and formulas are in the notebook and PDF. Review the AI disclosure and understand the work before individual submission.

Week 7 discussion guide¶

What problem did you solve? I used 70 stocks previously selected by SephWide to ask whether price-derived risk and behaviour features produce interpretable asset groups, then compared equal-weight portfolios over a later historical window. I did not measure actual funded trading results or change the trading system.

Why equities in a DeFi assignment? The title says DeFi, but the data requirement explicitly permits assets/tokens. I used the equity application to connect the method to my own signal project and disclosed the scope. A token-only interpretation would need the lecturer's agreement and a different dataset/calendar.

Did you select only winners? No. I froze all 72 distinct BUY names recorded by 1 September. Two failed data/identity checks, leaving 70. The requested five positive examples are a separate retrospective table; 46 negative outcomes remain visible.

Why exclude GOLD? A ticker is not a permanent company identity. Barrick changed from GOLD to B, and Gold.com later reused GOLD. I could not establish which issuer the strategy intended from this export, so I excluded it rather than combine companies. I retained the earlier result and disclosed that this correction followed inspection.

What is a row in PCA? One asset. Columns are eight features calculated from formation-period daily returns. Clustering daily dates would classify market regimes, not create groups of stocks.

Why standardize? Volatility, skewness and beta have different scales. Without scaling, Euclidean distance can be dominated by large numerical units. Correlated risk features still receive substantial collective influence, which is a limitation.

What does 82.71% mean? Three principal directions retain 82.71% of variation in the standardized asset-feature matrix. It does not mean 82.71% of future returns are explained, forecast correctly, or profitable.

What do the PCs represent? PC1 mainly separates higher-volatility, higher-beta, larger-downside stocks from less risky stocks. PC2 and PC3 combine persistence, market correlation, skewness and drawdown. Signs are arbitrary and economic labels are descriptive, not causal laws.

Why two clusters when the elbow suggests three? The declared choice maximizes training silhouette subject to at least three stocks per cluster. k=3 creates a singleton and fails that constraint. The selected silhouette is 0.3881, a diagnostic of separation, not proof of an optimal investment strategy.

What are the groups? Cluster 1 has 47 stocks and lower median formation-period volatility/beta; Cluster 2 has 23 stocks and higher risk. These labels are relative to this selected stock sample, not promises of low absolute risk.

What happened later? In 35 sessions after formation, net cumulative returns at assumed 10 bps one-way costs were -1.84% and -2.96%, versus SPY +1.53%. The portfolio test therefore does not demonstrate an advantage, despite individual successful signals.

Why does the less negative-return cluster have a worse Sharpe? Sharpe measures mean excess return divided by variability, not cumulative return. A modest negative excess mean divided by much smaller volatility can yield a more negative ratio. Both cluster intervals include zero, and 35 sessions are far too short for confident ranking. Always read the saved Sharpe together with its 85% interval.

Why not call this a clean out-of-sample proof? Features and model selection use earlier dates, but membership comes from my later strategy history, prior project knowledge exists, and the identity correction followed first-result inspection. The split is chronologically separated but conditional and retrospective.

Why MRNA as an example? Its first recorded BUY predates a very large price rise, and an issuer announcement gives dated clinical-trial context. This does not prove the model anticipated the announcement. Its hypothetical holding starts after the signal and ignores real strategy exits, costs and sizing.

What do the checks prove? They reconcile calculations and enforce the stated rules. They do not prove the vendor data are flawless, the model has predictive skill, the work is independently audited, or the approach should move real money.

What would you do next? Predeclare a genuinely future cohort, verify price and issuer identity against independent records, include dead/rejected stocks, measure execution costs and temporal cluster stability, and collect a much longer record. from this folder, and Run All. Frozen CSV inputs make the notebook work offline. prepare_data.py documents the one-time public Yahoo Finance download and the read-only project export; it is not needed to reproduce the submitted results. refresh_prices.py can make a separately named public-data refresh without access to SephWide. A refresh is a new data vintage and may change results.

Integrity and attribution: analysis/code drafted with OpenAI Codex assistance, with numerical checks included. The prompt record is supplied. The submission is individual; the student must understand and review it under the course's AI policy. No claim is made that generated work was independently authored without assistance.

Part 1.1 | Data collection and preprocessing (15 points)¶

Yahoo Finance daily adjusted close prices are downloaded through yfinance with auto_adjust=True: these are adjusted-price return proxies, not executable trade quotes. SPY is an equity market comparator. Sector labels are a dated local metadata snapshot used only to interpret the clusters. Signal timestamps establish recorded membership, not original vendor availability or broker execution.

Rules: use SPY's observed session dates; require at least 99% fit-period price coverage and exact first/last fit prices. Allow at most two consecutive missing prices, filled forward using only earlier observations. Never backfill or interpolate. Exclude invalid/insufficient fit histories with a reason; all admitted stocks must then have usable later data or execution stops. No stock is admitted/excluded based on later return. Large daily moves are flagged for review, never automatically erased.

Complete record: 24 positive, 46 negative and 0 flat price outcomes among 70 included names. Entries have different holding lengths and overlap. This is not a calibrated win probability, and transaction costs and actual strategy exits are absent here.

The 70-asset sample reduces from eight features to 3 PCs, retaining 82.7% of training variance. The chosen 2-cluster partition has silhouette 0.388; the inertia elbow suggests k=3. These are training diagnostics, not a profit forecast.

Cluster 1 contains 47 stocks, led by Utilities (7), Consumer Defensive (6). Its median training volatility is 30.3%, market beta 0.76, and drawdown -34.0%. In the later window its costed equal-weight portfolio returns -1.82%, with annualized volatility 9.6%, maximum drawdown -6.4%, and Sharpe -1.65 [-5.88, 2.39] (85% interval). The shared risk/sector exposures describe a plausible common sensitivity; a causal explanation would require dated event and factor evidence.

Cluster 2 contains 23 stocks, led by Unknown (13), Technology (5). Its median training volatility is 58.0%, market beta 1.68, and drawdown -62.4%. In the later window its costed equal-weight portfolio returns -2.96%, with annualized volatility 32.8%, maximum drawdown -13.4%, and Sharpe -0.59 [-5.06, 4.40] (85% interval). The shared risk/sector exposures describe a plausible common sensitivity; a causal explanation would require dated event and factor evidence.

Cluster 1 is the realized return leader (-1.82%); Cluster 2 is the laggard (-2.96%). These labels were assigned after the comparison and cannot justify picking the leader in advance. Portfolio diversification reduces idiosyncratic exposure, but clusters can remain correlated and a small group can concentrate sector risk.

Feature matrix: assets are the observations¶

Clustering dates would answer the wrong question. Here each row is one asset and each column is a summary of its fit-period daily adjusted-price returns: annualized mean, annualized sample volatility, downside deviation from zero, sample skewness, maximum drawdown, SPY beta, SPY correlation and lag-one autocorrelation. All eight features derive from the required prices. Downside deviation is sqrt(252 * mean(min(r,0)^2)); beta is cov(r,SPY)/var(SPY). Price levels are not comparable across differently priced shares, so returns are used instead. StandardScaler centers/scales each feature across training assets. The correlated risk features deliberately permit economic interpretation, but may overweight the common risk dimension. No later returns enter these features.

In [3]:
def max_drawdown(r):
    wealth = np.r_[1., np.cumprod(1 + np.asarray(r, dtype=float))]
    return float(np.min(wealth / np.maximum.accumulate(wealth) - 1))

def asset_features(returns):
    market = returns['SPY']
    result = {}
    for ticker in admitted:
        r = returns[ticker]
        result[ticker] = {
            'mean_ann': r.mean() * ANN,
            'vol_ann': r.std(ddof=1) * np.sqrt(ANN),
            'downside_ann': np.sqrt(np.minimum(r, 0).pow(2).mean() * ANN),
            'skew': r.skew(), 'max_drawdown': max_drawdown(r),
            'beta_spy': r.cov(market) / market.var(ddof=1),
            'corr_spy': r.corr(market), 'autocorr1': r.autocorr(1)}
    return pd.DataFrame.from_dict(result, orient='index')[CFG['features']]

Part 1.2 | Principal component analysis (15 points)¶

Full-SVD PCA operates on the standardized asset-by-feature matrix. Retain the smallest number of components explaining at least 80% of training cross-sectional variance, a rule declared before performance evaluation. This balances compression and information retention; it is not a claim of a unique optimal dimension. PCA is centered, unwhitened and linear. K-Means uses all retained scores, so components with more variance carry more weight. The charts may show only the first two/three. Component signs are arbitrary; interpretations use joint feature directions.

In [4]:

Part 1.3 | K-Means clustering (20 points)¶

Test the declared grid k=2,…,8, k-means++, 50 initializations, seed 42. The elbow is an inertia diagnostic: the largest normalized distance below the chord joining k=1 and k=8. Selection uses maximum silhouette among solutions with at least three assets per cluster, breaking ties toward smaller k. The size constraint avoids presenting single-stock outliers as diversified portfolios. The elbow can disagree; both are reported rather than selecting on later returns. K-Means minimizes within-cluster squared Euclidean distance. It assumes roughly compact groups, is sensitive to outliers and imposes a hard partition on continuous financial characteristics. Silhouette separation is not investment performance.

In [5]:

for k in CFG['k_grid']:
    model = KMeans(n_clusters=k, n_init=50, random_state=SEED).fit(Z)
    sizes = np.bincount(model.labels_, minlength=k)
    models[k] = model
    trials.append({'k': k, 'inertia': model.inertia_,

Cluster validation and full attempt accounting¶

Twenty additional seeds at the selected k are fitted on the same training scores. Adjusted Rand index (ARI) compares partitions independently of arbitrary label numbers. This measures optimizer sensitivity, not stability across future regimes. For this final data version the attempt ledger records one k=1 elbow baseline, seven candidate-k fits and twenty seed checks: 28 fits, each with 50 initialization restarts (1,400 starts). An earlier 71-asset version was calculated before the GOLD identity exclusion; its notebook/results are retained under validation. Across both data versions: 56 fits and 2,800 starts. The data correction happened after initial result inspection; this comparison is not an untouched holdout. No failed/ineligible candidate is deleted. These unsupervised comparisons do not constitute 28 independent tests of profitability.

    stability.append({'seed': seed, 'ari_vs_selected': adjusted_rand_score(model.labels_, other.labels_),
                      'inertia': other.inertia_})

Part 2.1 | Portfolio construction (10 points)¶

Each cluster starts with equal weights 1/n_cluster. Equal weights avoid estimating expected-return inputs from this small, selected sample. Holdings rebalance daily to those fixed targets. We also show: (i) equal weights across all admitted assets; (ii) equal capital across clusters, equal weights within each; (iii) SPY. The equal-cluster allocation is fixed before later performance is inspected; it overweights small clusters relative to the all-asset comparator. Every target weight is supplied, including this concentration effect. These are educational portfolios constructed here, not historical SephWide allocations or trade replay.

Costs: 10 basis points per unit of one-way traded notional, including initial purchases, drift-rebalancing and final liquidation. One-way turnover is sum(abs(target_weight - drifted_weight)), not half that sum. Costs are applied multiplicatively to wealth. The small reduction in invested notional needed to pay fees is approximated by the turnover charge; an exact self-financing impact model is outside this exercise. Sensitivities of 0 and 25 bps are reported without changing portfolio design. Taxes, spread variation, market impact, capacity and borrow are not modeled. All positions are long-only with no leverage.

In [8]:

def simulate(asset_returns, target, cost_bps=10):
    target = np.asarray(target, dtype=float)
    r = np.asarray(asset_returns, dtype=float)
    check('Simulator input alignment and finite returns', r.shape[1] == len(target) and np.isfinite(r).all())
    check('Simulator weights valid', np.isclose(target.sum(), 1) and np.min(target) >= 0)
    gross = r @ target
    turnover = np.empty(len(r)); turnover[0] = np.abs(target).sum()
    for t in range(1, len(r)):
        drift = target * (1 + r[t-1]) / (1 + gross[t-1])
        turnover[t] = np.abs(target - drift).sum()
    fee = cost_bps / 10000
    net = (1 - fee * turnover) * (1 + gross) - 1
    net[-1] = (1 + net[-1]) * (1 - fee) - 1  # liquidate once, at the end
    return net, turnover

later, turns = {}, {}
for name in weights:
    later[name], turns[name] = simulate(test[admitted], weights[name], 10)
later['SPY'], turns['SPY'] = simulate(test[['SPY']], [1.], 10)
later = pd.DataFrame(later, index=test.index)
turns = pd.DataFrame(turns, index=test.index)

turns.to_csv(OUT / 'comparison_one_way_turnover.csv', index_label='Date')

Part 2.2 | Performance metrics and uncertainty (15 points)¶

For net simple daily returns r, equity is cumprod(1+r) and cumulative return is final equity minus one. Annualized volatility uses sample standard deviation times sqrt(252). Sharpe is sqrt(252) * mean(r-rf_daily) / std(r-rf_daily), with 3% annual risk-free assumption converted by (1.03)^(1/252)-1. This is an explicit constant assumption, not a downloaded historical cash yield. Maximum drawdown includes initial wealth 1, so a first-day loss is counted.

Beta is the sample covariance of portfolio and gross adjusted SPY excess returns divided by benchmark variance. Alpha is 252 * (mean(portfolio excess) - beta * mean(SPY excess)), an arithmetic annualized regression intercept. It is reported with an 85% circular-block-bootstrap interval, not interpreted as proven alpha. SPY's net portfolio is shown for fair cost comparison; regression uses gross SPY.

Every displayed Sharpe includes an 85% percentile interval from 2,000 circular moving-block resamples of length five. Portfolio/market pairs are resampled together for alpha. These intervals condition on the selected assets, fixed clusters and this short regime; they ignore universe/model-selection uncertainty and are not simultaneous or anytime-valid intervals. No annualized return extrapolation is used to claim a year of observed profit.

In [9]:
def performance(r, market):
    r = np.asarray(r, dtype=float); market = np.asarray(market, dtype=float)
    excess, mx = r - RF, market - RF
    sd = excess.std(ddof=1)
    beta = np.cov(excess, mx, ddof=1)[0, 1] / mx.var(ddof=1)
    return {'cumulative_return': np.prod(1 + r) - 1,
            'vol_ann': r.std(ddof=1) * np.sqrt(ANN),
            'max_drawdown': max_drawdown(r),
            'sharpe': np.sqrt(ANN) * excess.mean() / sd if sd > 0 else np.nan,
            'beta': beta, 'alpha_ann': ANN * (excess.mean() - beta * mx.mean())}

def block_intervals(r, market, seed=42, repetitions=2000, block=5):
    r, m = np.asarray(r), np.asarray(market)
    n = len(r); rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    starts = rng.integers(0, n, (repetitions, int(np.ceil(n / block))))
    ix = ((starts[..., None] + np.arange(block)) % n).reshape(repetitions, -1)[:, :n]
    a, b = r[ix] - RF, m[ix] - RF
    sd = a.std(axis=1, ddof=1)
    sr = np.divide(a.mean(axis=1) * np.sqrt(ANN), sd,
                   out=np.full(repetitions, np.nan), where=sd > 0)
    ac, bc = a - a.mean(axis=1, keepdims=True), b - b.mean(axis=1, keepdims=True)
    beta = (ac * bc).sum(axis=1) / (bc * bc).sum(axis=1)
    alpha = ANN * (a.mean(axis=1) - beta * b.mean(axis=1))
    return np.nanquantile(sr, [.075, .925]), np.nanquantile(alpha, [.075, .925])

metrics = []
for name in later:
    row = performance(later[name], test.SPY)
    sr_ci, alpha_ci = block_intervals(later[name], test.SPY)
    row.update({'portfolio': name, 'sharpe_low85': sr_ci[0], 'sharpe_high85': sr_ci[1],
                'alpha_low85': alpha_ci[0], 'alpha_high85': alpha_ci[1],
                'one_way_notional_turnover': turns[name].sum() + 1, 'n_sessions': len(test)})
    metrics.append(row)
metrics = pd.DataFrame(metrics).set_index('portfolio')
metrics.to_csv(OUT / 'performance_metrics.csv')
readable = pd.DataFrame(index=metrics.index)
for col in ['cumulative_return', 'vol_ann', 'max_drawdown']:
    readable[col] = metrics[col].map(lambda x: f'{x:.2%}')
readable['Sharpe [85% interval]'] = [f'{r.sharpe:.2f} [{r.sharpe_low85:.2f}, {r.sharpe_high85:.2f}]' for r in metrics.itertuples()]
readable['beta'] = metrics.beta.round(2)
readable['alpha ann [85% interval]'] = [f'{r.alpha_ann:.1%} [{r.alpha_low85:.1%}, {r.alpha_high85:.1%}]' for r in metrics.itertuples()]
display(readable)
say(f'All metrics use the same **{len(test)} sessions**. Annualized Sharpe/alpha '

    'does not turn a historical winner into an investable discovery.')

SephWide connection | Recorded signals that subsequently rose¶

This is a separate retrospective illustration, requested for the project link. For every frozen BUY name, use the first recorded BUY date, then the first available adjusted close strictly after that date (never the possibly partial signal-day close), and compare it with the final adjusted close on 21 October. The table retains positive and negative cases and records entry/end dates.

The top five positive returns are displayed as successful examples chosen after observing the outcome. This selection is not evidence of overall predictive skill. The baseline is a hypothetical close-to-end long position with matching SPY dates; it ignores SephWide exits/top-ups/position sizing and is not its realized return. The frozen main asset sample was not filtered using this table. Raw trade-log prices are deliberately not treated as verified executions.

Part 3.1 | Results interpretation (8 points)¶

The following commentary is generated from the measured tables. Training profiles explain economic grouping; later returns describe one realized market window. Sector composition can support a mechanism hypothesis, but this dataset alone cannot identify the news, valuation change or macro shock that caused a return.

Part 3.2 | Investment insights and allocation strategies (7 points)¶

  1. Use clusters as an exposure map. Before adding another SephWide name, inspect whether it repeats an existing high-volatility/high-beta or sector exposure. This is a research interpretation, not a change to SephWide's production rules.
  2. Compare the two allocation policies already specified. Equal capital across clusters reduces domination by the largest cluster but increases weights in small clusters. Equal weights across all stocks can be more balanced at the individual security level. The weight table makes this trade-off explicit.
  3. For a risk-constrained mandate, investigate a lower-volatility cluster or explicit risk budgets using training data and a separate future validation. A low historical volatility estimate does not establish low future risk. Check individual-name and sector concentration, liquidity, and portfolio correlations.
  4. Do not chase the measured leader or the five successful signal examples. Later ranking and conditional Sharpe intervals cannot establish a lasting risk-adjusted advantage. The actionable next step is to freeze this workflow and record future results before considering capital allocation or any strategy change.

The numerical equal-cluster and all-asset allocations are implementable research examples. No live adoption is recommended from this short retrospective comparison.

Part 3.3 | Limitations and improvements (5 points)¶

  • Selection and survivorship: these are stocks selected by a strategy in August/ September 2026. Requiring sufficient price history also favors seasoned survivors. Results cannot describe the full historical opportunity set, dead stocks or the strategy's skill before these selections. Formation-date membership is fixed before later returns, but the overall study remains retrospective and informed by the project.
  • Data vintage/quality: Yahoo adjusted closes may be revised and back-adjusted; no contemporaneous vendor vintage is claimed. SPY's observed dates are the calendar reference, not an independently certified exchange calendar. Forward fills can create zero returns and distort volatility. Corporate actions, symbol reuse and large moves need independent exchange/issuer verification. Sector labels are a snapshot and may be stale. No price or signal timestamp is a broker-fill receipt.
  • Short, dependent comparison: only several weeks of later data, overlapping signal holding periods and one market regime. Annualization amplifies sampling noise. Five-session block bootstrap assumes locally repeatable dependence and does not capture every tail risk. Its 85% intervals condition on fixed selection/models; inspecting multiple clusters makes leader estimates optimistic. No multiplicity- adjusted alpha significance or strategy superiority is claimed.
  • Model assumptions: linear PCA can miss nonlinear structure; scale choices and correlated features alter distances. K-Means assumes compact Euclidean groups, and outliers or small sample size can dominate. Silhouette and the elbow need not agree. Optimizer-seed stability is distinct from temporal stability. Features and cluster membership may change with market conditions.
  • Portfolio assumptions: daily equal-weight rebalancing, fractional shares, adjusted-price return proxies, fixed friction and fixed risk-free rate. Execution timing, taxes, funding, liquidity, capacity, variable spread and market impact remain unmeasured. Alpha/beta use only SPY, so omitted factors can explain residuals.
  • Scope: US equities demonstrate the asset workflow permitted by the text, not DeFi token behavior. Tokens would require 365-day annualization, 24/7 calendar, exchange/chain risks, staking/yield definitions, depegs and delisted-token coverage.
  • Next work: freeze an independent future cohort; retain rejected/delisted names; verify corporate actions and data against another source; use a much longer forward record; assess rolling stability and robust scaling using training data; validate realistic execution costs and rebalance frequency. Any variants must be declared and counted rather than selected on this comparison window.

The cover says “Before Week 8 or Week 9 Session,” whereas the body and final line say “Before Week 8 Session.” Treat before Week 8 as the working deadline and confirm the calendar date with the lecturer. The brief states “100 (+30 bonus)” but gives no bonus tasks or marking criteria. This notebook addresses the explicit 100-point rubric; it does not invent a bonus requirement or reuse Week 6's cell cap.

Verification and submission checklist¶

The independent audit script checks formulas with separate calculations, data hashes, chronology, k-selection, exact weights, portfolio compounding, transaction costs, and output completeness. The in-notebook policy checks below are structural checks, not passed hypotheses of profitability. No project tests or agents run.
